title: Auditable routing evidence spec for region pins
content:
Purpose

This doc defines the minimum evidence surface and operational controls required to demonstrate to internal auditors and customer compliance teams that region pinning rules were enforced for a given customer request. Focus is on high-signal artifacts which map routing decisions to contractual residency obligations, and on pragmatic retention/aggregation that balances auditability and storage cost.

Scope and audience

Scope: hosted and private control plane routing decisions for requests that have been tagged as region-pinned (customer-level or per-request). Includes fallback routing events, routing overrides, and model variant substitution where region constraints apply.
Audience: eng-private-deployments, platform-observability, legal/compliance reviewers, customer success escalation engineers.

High-level requirements

1) Traceability: Each routed request must be associated with a trace id and the following fields captured in a tamper-resistant log stream: timestamp_utc, trace_id, customer_id, customer_contract_region (canonical country/region code), effective_region (where inference executed), routing_policy_id, policy_version, route_decision_reason, fallback_flag (true/false), operator_override_id (if set), model_variant_id, infra_zone_id, and request_digest (sha256).

2) Immutability and signing: Logs used for audit evidence must be exported to an append-only storage tier. For hosted customers, daily exports to a cold store with a rolling HMAC ledger are sufficient. For Private deployments, guidance is to enable local append-only logs and a periodic signed manifest that can be shipped to the customer or compliance team.

3) Retention windows: Raw request-level evidence should be stored for 90 days by default. Aggregated summaries and manifests for audit replay must be retained for 3 years for enterprise customers with contractual obligations. Retention overrides should be gated behind legal approvals and documented per customer.

4) Reproductionability: It must be possible to reconstruct the routing decision for a request using retained inputs. Inputs required include routing policy id/version, the canonical customer residency mapping at the time of request, and infra zone mapping.

Artifact types (what we will produce)

- Live routing event record (high cardinality): one record per routed request with the fields listed under Traceability. Stored in internal telemetry stream with export hooks.
- Daily signed manifest: a digest for the day's routing events with counts by region, by policy version, and by fallback type. Signed by platform key and checkpointed.
- Repro playbook bundle: for audit cases we export a small bundle per sample request that contains: the routing event record, policy snapshot, infra zone inventory at time T, and anonymized request digest.
- Operator audit log: captures manual overrides, who made them, and associated justification text.

Example high-signal log line (plain text, avoid exposing payload):

2024-08-29T14:22:11Z | trace=trc_0a3f9 | cust=acct-314 | contract_region=eu | effective_region=eu-west1 | policy=id=pin-v2 v=2024-06-12 | reason=pin-match | fallback=false | override=none | model=llama-70b-q4f | zone=eu-west1-a | digest=sha256:9f2c...

Operational checklist for onboarding a pinned customer

- Confirm contractual residency requirement and canonical region code entry in customer metadata.
- Create/assign a routing policy id and set policy_version. Link the policy id to Confluence page and Jira for changelog.
- Enable verbose routing telemetry for first 72 hours post-onboarding.
- Configure daily manifest exports and sign key rotation schedule.
- Run sample replay tests (see replay checklist) and produce a small reproducibility bundle for the initial audit.

Replay checklist (how an auditor can verify a sample)

1) Provide trace id(s) to platform team.
2) Platform exports the routing event record and the day's signed manifest.
3) Verify manifest signature and counts.
4) Reconstruct routing decision using saved policy snapshot and infra map; the reconstructed effective_region must match stored effective_region.
4a) If fallback_flag=true, reproduce the fallback trigger using simulated capacity signals if possible.

Acceptance criteria for evidence package

- All fields from the traceability list present and non-empty.
- Digest matches the anonymized request hash stored in internal request logs.
- Manifest signature verifies against platform public key.
- Reconstructed decision matches recorded decision, or a documented divergence exists with operator justification.

Telemetry/implementation notes for engineers

- Prefer structured key-value log records in our telemetry pipeline; keep the field names stable and documented in the schema registry. Avoid changing policy_version semantics without issuing a migration plan.
- For on-hosted control plane: route decisions should be emitted synchronously as part of the routing path to avoid race conditions. For Private deployments, provide a local emitter that writes to append-only storage and also forwards a digest to central observability (where policy permits).
- To limit storage, we will keep full request records for 90 days and produce compressed daily manifests after 7 days. Manifests are the primary long-term artifact for auditors.

Security and privacy considerations

- Do not include PII or request payload in the routing evidence. Use an anonymized request_digest to link to internal request logs when legally permissible.
- For EU customers with strict residency, ensure exports of manifests and playbooks do not leave the EU unless contractually approved.

Open questions / decisions needed

- Ledger approach: HMAC-based daily ledger vs. chained-signed manifests. Preference: HMAC ledger for simplicity, but security should sign off.
- Retention override workflow: need legal-approved template.
- Operator override tagging: must we capture a PR link or support ticket id for every manual route change? (recommended yes)

Next steps and owners

- implement schema changes in telemetry pipeline (owner: Mateo) - target sprint 2024-09-15
- proto daily manifest exporter and signer (owner: Li Wei) - prototype by 2024-08-30
- draft legal retention template and export approval flow (owner: Aisha) - draft by 2024-09-08

Notes to reviewers

This is intentionally pragmatic: auditors want repeatable, verifiable artifacts, not full request payloads. If a customer requires deeper replay (payload-level), route that request through the enterprise legal/onboarding process. Feedback welcome on tradeoffs between longer raw retention and operational cost.
